docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
CAPM is a package manager for all tools related code analysis. It provides a single command to find, run, and configure your code analysis tools.

For example, running the tokei code counter is as simple as: capm run tokei:

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
Code analysis should be easy and one of the first things to set up for a software project, not an afterthought.

Static analysis tools give insight into code metrics such as volume, complexity, and duplication. CAPM makes running these tools from the CLI, and GitHub Actions, straightforward.

docs.title: How
docs.text: CAPM wraps static analysis tools in a small Docker image, called packages. It also provides a CLI command and GitHub Action to run these packages.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
After installing dependencies with uv sync, CAPM can be run from the repository root like this:

uv run capm

For example, to run the tokei package, run:

uv run capm run tokei

docs.title: Local installation using pipx
docs.text:
To install the development repository locally in editable mode run:

pipx install --force --editable .

To install the main branch locally run:

pipx install git+https://github.com/getcapm/capm.git

Or to install another branch locally run:

pip install git+https://github.com/getcapm/capm.git@issue-123

docs.title: Building the binary distribution
docs.text:
Generate a self-contained binary:

uv run poe bundle

docs.title: Static documentation
docs.text:
Generating the static documentation:

uv run mkdocs build

See the output:

uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Running a package
docs.text:
The run command runs a package inside the current directory.

For example, to show the help screen for JSHint (a linter for JavaScript):

capm run jshint --help

Only the first time a package is used, CAPM will build the Docker image.

To run JSHint on the src directory:

capm run jshint src

Specific package configuration files are not managed by CAPM and can be stored in the codebase as usual.

docs.title: Package configuration
docs.text:
A file called .capm.yml can be used to configure multiple packages, for example:

packages:
  - mypy
  - ruff

New packages can be added using the capm add command. Packages can be removed using the capm remove command. Packages can be listed using the capm list command`

docs.title: Finding packages
docs.text: A list of packages can be found on the Packages page.

docs.title: Running in GitHub Actions
docs.text:
There's a GitHub Action available (capm-action) that you can add to your CI workflow. This action will run all configured CAPM packages.

An example of a GitHub Actions workflow using the CAPM action:

name: code-analysis

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  code_analysis:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout sources
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Run CAPM
        uses: getcapm/capm-action@v1

docs.title: Homebrew
docs.text:
CAPM is available for Homebrew:

brew install getcapm/capm/capm

docs.title: Pipx
docs.text:
To install the standalone version of CAPM in an isolated Python environment using pipx run:

pipx install capm

docs.title: PyPi
docs.text:
To install the standalone version of CAPM for your default Python installation run:

python -m pip install capm

docs.title: Platform binaries
docs.text: Binaries for different platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows) are available on the latest release page.
